QB have an 8UI period; adjacent phases are 2UI apart (only I↔IB and Q↔QB are 4UI apart).<br>• Cells 0/1 use I/IB, so mux[0] and mux[1] switch on I edges. Cells 2/3 use Q/QB, so mux[2] and mux[3] switch 2UI later, as in Fig. 4.<br>• DFF: rising-edge flip-flop. <b>LAT: transparent while EN = 1</b>; it delays the "0" input by half a period (4UI). MUX: passes input "1" while sel = 1, input "0" otherwise.<br>• Output order: mux[0] = d0, d4, d8, …; mux[1] = d1, d5, …; mux[2] = d2, d6, …; mux[3] = d3, d7, …<br>• Inside the 8:4, each data edge is launched by the same clock edge that ends its selection: ≈4UI of setup-side slack, ≈t<sub>cq</sub> of hold-side slack.<br>• PI/PD lock drawn with p0/p2 centred on mux[0]/mux[2]; the ~1UI dly div.div: Ret. & 8:4 serializer — timing of one bit-slice (8 lanes × 1 bit of the 8×11b bus)

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 1438px; height: 1px; padding-top: 31px; margin-left: 5px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #555555;

div.div: Context: Cusmai et al., ISSCC 2024 (7.2) / JSSC 2025, Figs. 1 and 4. Internal structure DFF → latch → 2:1 MUX is an assumed implementation; each stage is drawn with td ≈ 0.25 UI.

div.div:
Notes
• I, Q, IB, QB have an 8UI period; adjacent phases are 2UI apart (only I↔IB and Q↔QB are 4UI apart).
• Cells 0/1 use I/IB, so mux[0] and mux[1] switch on I edges. Cells 2/3 use Q/QB, so mux[2] and mux[3] switch 2UI later, as in Fig. 4.
• DFF: rising-edge flip-flop. LAT: transparent while EN = 1; it delays the "0" input by half a period (4UI). MUX: passes input "1" while sel = 1, input "0" otherwise.
• Output order: mux[0] = d0, d4, d8, …; mux[1] = d1, d5, …; mux[2] = d2, d6, …; mux[3] = d3, d7, …
• Inside the 8:4, each data edge is launched by the same clock edge that ends its selection: ≈4UI of setup-side slack, ≈tcq of hold-side slack.
• PI/PD lock drawn with p0/p2 centred on mux[0]/mux[2]; the ~1UI dly re-centres mux[1]/mux[3] (red arrows: 0.5UI → 1.5UI).
